Thinking about the cost of living in Vancouver, especially food and transportation. Vancouver is known to be expensive, and I want to budget accordingly.

Groceries in Vancouver can vary depending on dietary preferences and lifestyle, with a rough estimate of $10-15 CAD per week for basic fruits and vegetables, $20-30 CAD per week for protein sources and dairy products, and $20-30 CAD per month for rice, pasta, canned goods, and snacks.
Eating out in Vancouver can range from $15-30 CAD per meal for casual dining, and $30-50 CAD per meal for mid-range restaurants. High-end restaurants can cost $50-100 CAD per meal or more.

Public transit in Vancouver is a comprehensive system including buses, SkyTrain, and SeaBus. A single ride costs $3.15 CAD, but you can purchase a monthly pass for $95.20 CAD or a student pass for $78.20 CAD.
Biking is a bike-friendly option in Vancouver, and you can purchase a used bike or rent one for a few hours or days.
Car sharing or ride-hailing services like Modo or Zipcar can be a cost-effective option for occasional use. Ride-hailing services like Uber or Lyft are also available, but prices can add up quickly.

The cost of rent in Vancouver varies depending on location, size, and amenities, with a shared apartment costing around $1,500-2,500 CAD per month and a one-bedroom apartment costing around $2,000-4,000 CAD per month.
Utilities in Vancouver include electricity, water, and internet, with a cost of around $100-200 CAD per month.
Vancouver offers many free or low-cost activities, such as hiking, visiting museums, or attending outdoor events. However, you may want to budget for occasional concerts, movies, or sporting events.
